article.articleHeadline: Bacterium that threatens tilapia farming advances into new regions of Brazil.

Overall S. agalactiae was detected in 39 of 309 analyses (13%), while serotype Ib had 28 positives in 156 analyses (17.9%). Co-circulation of serotypes underscores sanitation strategies must consider farm history and regional epidemiology. Clinical signs include anorexia, lethargy, erratic swimming, exophthalmia, corneal opacity, neurological changes, systemic inflammation, and mortality. Vaccination is a principal preventive tool; commercial vaccines offer defined antigen content and dosing when properly used, but effectiveness depends on administration, water quality, animal condition, and timing relative to exposure. Vaccination should be integrated with biosafety: PCR diagnostics, serotyping, origin, stocking density, water quality, equipment hygiene, and stress reduction. In areas with serotype III presence or risk of introduction due to fish movement, preemptive vaccination is more robust than waiting for outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: Tiny Vesicles Reveal How Toxoplasma gondii Quietly Rewires Its Host
article.articleSummary: Toxoplasma gondii, a globally widespread single-celled parasite infecting billions, communicates with its host not only through rhoptry, microneme, and dense granule secretion but via extracellular vesicles (EVs) that function as a parallel signaling axis. A Parasites & Vectors review led by Erick Fonseca Balbino and Izadora Volpato Rossi from Brazilian institutions (State University of Londrina; Federal University of Uberlândia; Federal University of Triângulo Mineiro; Fiocruz Carlos Chagas Institute) argues EVs extend the parasite’s secretory toolkit, carrying parasite- and host-derived cargo, including rhoptry/microneme/dense granule proteins, regulatory microRNAs, and bioactive lipids. EVs are produced using conserved eukaryotic machinery (ESCRT, SNARE) in parasite multivesicular bodies, generating vesicles reflecting both parasite and host physiology. Functional themes include infection priming, immune modulation (dampened Th1 signaling and tolerance), and neural reprogramming, contributing to lifelong persistence. Characterization relies on ultracentrifugation, size-exclusion chromatography, nanoparticle tracking, electron microscopy, mass spectrometry, Western blot, and lipidomics.

article.articleHeadline: Bahia Public Prosecutor's Office identifies fecal bacteria in the water of a quilombola community in Chapada Diamantina.
article.articleSummary: In Bahia, Brazil, the Public Prosecutor’s Office identifies fecal contamination in water from Comunidade Quilombola Queimada Nova, Morro do Chapéu, Chapada Diamantina. Technical reports find total coliforms in cisterns, the well network, and the local desalination system, with Escherichia coli detected in desalinated water, indicating fecal pollution. The regional groundwater shows elevated sulfur and high salinity, worsened by chronic drought, lack of sewage infrastructure, and improper open-dump waste disposal. The MP-BA opened investigations, formally requesting Morro do Chapéu’s municipal authorities to provide maintenance plans for wells and the desalination unit, the schedule for water trucks, sanitation solutions, and waste management. Embasa is asked to assess the feasibility of expanding the water network. Emergency measures include distributing sodium hypochlorite and diarrhea-control actions, health impact assessments, risk mitigation for flood-prone homes, official recognition of the quilombola school, CadÚnico updates, and strengthened food security programs. Signed by Gabriela Gomes Cerqueira Ferreira (Regional Environmental Prosecutor, Jacobina).

article.articleHeadline: Malaria: understand the risks, symptoms, and the importance of early diagnosis.
article.articleSummary: Malaria, caused by Plasmodium and transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes, remains a persistent public health challenge in Brazil, including Amazon regions. Incubation around 8–14 days after a female Anopheles bite. Classic symptoms: high fever with cycles, severe chills, sweating, muscle aches, and persistent headache; later nausea, vomiting, fatigue. Diagnosis relies mainly on thick blood smear microscopy to detect parasite and identify species; Brazil's public health system (SUS) provides free, rapid diagnosis and treatment. Treatment uses antimalarials such as chloroquine and primaquine, with dosage tailored to patient and severity; adherence is essential to prevent relapse and serious complications like severe anemia, renal failure, or neurological issues. Prevention focuses on vector avoidance: repellents, window screens, clothing, and environmental control, especially at dusk and at night when Anopheles are active. The article highlights risks and emphasizes early diagnosis.

article.articleHeadline: Adults with dengue admitted to public health system ICUs in a more severe condition than those in the private health system.
article.articleSummary: Adults with dengue admitted to Brazil’s public health system ICUs are in more severe condition than those in private hospitals, per a Journal of Critical Care study (2015–2024). Public-system patients had 20% intubation on day one in ICU vs 4% in private facilities. Researchers from Einstein Hospital Israelita and IDOR link greater severity to delays in reaching intensive care. Data from the Brazilian ICU Registry and Datasus show overall ICU hospital mortality at 8.2%; public hospitals recorded 3,682 admissions and 889 deaths, while private hospitals had 28,334 admissions and 1,704 deaths. Public patients were younger (median age 50 vs 54) yet more often required vasopressors on day one (22.4% vs 5.3%), with vasopressor-related mortality at 54.6%. Dengue is transmitted by female Aedes aegypti; LIRAa indicates substantial risk. A 2025 Anvisa single-dose Butantan dengue vaccine (12–59 years) is suspended due to safety concerns.

article.articleHeadline: Vigia de Nazaré confirms four cases of Chagas disease.
article.articleSummary: Four cases of Chagas disease were confirmed in Vigia de Nazaré, Pará, Brazil, prompting intensified prevention and surveillance at local açaí-selling points. The alert, disclosed Oct 6, 2026, aims to curb oral transmission from contaminated foods like açaí. A meeting with local açaí beaters is scheduled for Oct 9, 2026 to align processing with Sanitary Surveillance standards and ensure product safety. After notification by Instituto Evandro Chagas, the Pará state health department (Sespa) deployed technicians and mobilized staff to support outbreak control and ensure medicines for affected individuals. Sespa will train health professionals, provide preventive guidance to the population, and coordinate with Vigia’s municipal health department to draft a specific local plan. Prevention emphasizes buying from regulated establishments, checking food hygiene, and maintaining clean, insect-free environments. Transmission routes include insect feces and contaminated foods; diagnosis via specific tests; treatment available through SUS.

article.articleHeadline: Health authorities warn of two disease outbreaks among birds and rabbits in Ponta Delgada.
article.articleSummary: Newcastle disease in birds (pigeons and doves) and Rabbit Hemorrhagic Disease (RHD) outbreaks are reported in the municipality of Ponta Delgada, São Miguel, Azores. About 40–50 fatalities per day; Newcastle has persisted for weeks with increasing wildlife deaths. RHD was detected roughly 1–2 weeks ago and is spreading in Capelas, Santo António, Livramento, and areas Fajã de Cima and Fajã de Baixa, with notable impact on the urban rabbit population in Ponta Delgada’s Urban Park. No human infection risk; transmission occurs within species. Correct response includes promptly burying carcasses and contacting the parish or Municipal Health Authority for guidance. Domestic rabbit and bird owners are urged to adopt preventive measures and consider vaccination. The origin of RHD is not yet identified; the disease recurs cyclically in São Miguel over the past two decades due to high density.

article.articleHeadline: State on alert for rabies prevention and reinforces precautions for dogs, cats, and bats | Tribuna de Petrópolis
article.articleSummary: Rabies alert in Rio de Janeiro state after August confirmation of a rabies case in a dog living in an urban area of the city of Rio de Janeiro, with history of bat exposure. In Petrópolis, authorities urge keeping dogs and cats vaccinated and avoiding contact with bats and wildlife; do not touch unknown animals. If a sick or dead bat is found, isolate it, cover with a bucket, cardboard box, or clean, dry cloth, and contact Environmental Surveillance. People should report animals showing signs such as abrupt behavior change, heavy salivation, lack of motor coordination, or progressive paralysis. If there is human exposure, wash the area with water and soap and seek urgent care, preferably at UPA Cascatinha. Vaccination is the main prevention; Petrópolis has carried out four vaccination campaigns this year, vaccinating 23,026 dogs and cats (72.4% coverage). Rabies is a deadly viral disease transmitted via saliva, nearly 100% fatal after symptoms. Environmental Surveillance unit: Rua Dr. Sá Earp, 433, Morin; phones: (24) 2231-0841 / 2291-1594 / 2291-1797.

article.articleHeadline: Travel-related dengue fever case reported on Oʻahu
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-09, Hawaiʻi Department of Health reports a new travel-related dengue fever case on Oʻahu, bringing Hawaii’s 2026 total to eight; all cases involve travel to Pacific Island countries/territories and show no link to prior Hawaiʻi cases. The infected individual acquired the virus while traveling in a dengue-endemic region. Health teams are conducting inspections and mosquito-control in the area; the risk of local transmission is low. Recent heavy rain highlights the need to eliminate standing water to reduce breeding. Dengue is a year-round risk in tropical/subtropical areas, including Central/South America (Brazil, Mexico), parts of Asia (Philippines), Africa, the Caribbean (Puerto Rico), and Pacific islands (American Samoa, FSM, Marshall Islands, Palau). Travelers should review country-specific guidance 4–6 weeks before travel, use EPA-registered repellents, wear protective clothing, and stay in screened or air-conditioned accommodations. Return travelers should prevent bites for 3 weeks and seek evaluation within 2 weeks if symptoms (fever, nausea, vomiting, rash, body aches) develop; report suspected cases at 808-586-4586.

article.articleHeadline: Tecpar grants the Seal of Innovation to the platform that monitors dengue, chikungunya, and Zika.
article.articleSummary: Tecpar, the Institute of Technology of Paraná, awarded the Selo de Inovação to EDL Brasil for the Plataforma Digital Integrada de Inteligência Territorial para Vigilância de Arboviroses, a system for dengue, chikungunya and Zika surveillance. The platform unites a field mobile app, a web portal, interactive dashboards, georeferencing, logistics, maintenance, routes, and epidemiological data in an offline-first environment to support public and private sector operations. Validated with municipal health secretaries and Tecpar’s campus, it currently monitors more than 1,500 georeferenced points nationwide, including seven active points at the Tecpar Campus CIC, with 23 more planned before summer—the peak period for vector reproduction. Linked to Estações Disseminadoras de Larvicida (EDLs) — smart traps that autodisseminate larvicide to hard-to-reach breeding sites—the platform tracks device locations and field activities, turning records into actionable data for decision-makers to improve disease control and resource use.

article.articleHeadline: An epidemiologist allowed the importation of Ebola into Russia.
article.articleSummary: Epidemiologist Gennady Onishchenko, academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences, says Ebola importation into Russia from the Democratic Republic of Congo is possible but would not spread domestically. In a TASS interview, he argued that while Ebola could be brought in, rapid detection would prevent transmission, and it is not transmitted via airborne droplets as SARS-CoV-2. Ebola spreads through close contact with the secretions of infected people. He noted the current outbreak is less active than the 2016 surge. August reports suggested the DRC outbreak could become the largest on record, and in October MSF warned that spread in North Kivu province in eastern DRC had gotten out of control. The article frames Russia as facing imported risk rather than ongoing domestic transmission.

article.articleHeadline: WHO Weekly Situation Update on Ongoing Health Emergency Events in South Sudan - Week #40, Date: 28 Sep - 4 Oct 2026 - South Sudan
article.articleSummary: Week 40 (28 Sep–4 Oct 2026) South Sudan update: Sustain BVD preparedness across 15 priority counties as DRC records 8,375 cases and Kenya reports its first imported case; PoE screening totals 72,183 (1–3 Oct) with continued readiness along the western corridor. Cholera response continues in Mayom and Renk, with a cumulative 112,186 cases and 15 new cases plus 1 death in Fangak; aim for 100% rapid diagnostic testing and an earliest end-of-outbreak declaration by 26 Oct. Poliovirus outbreak response accelerates with five new cVDPV1 and one new cVDPV2 case; cVDPV2 now extends to Awerial, Lakes; finalize R1 National Immunization Day readiness and address active measles outbreaks in Tonj North and Aweil South. Guinea Worm surveillance shows 0 human and animal cases in 2026, with 3 wild-cat detections in Week 40; continuing health education, water treatment, and pipe-filter distribution in affected communities.

article.articleHeadline: Kenya Red Cross supports response to country's first Ebola case
article.articleSummary: Kenya confirms its first Ebola case and first fatality, in Nairobi, involving a Kenyan national who had lived in Congo before returning home. The Kenya Red Cross is supporting the government's efforts to prevent a public health crisis, with Paul Olala, the NGO's head of health security and emergencies, coordinating the response. FRANCE 24's Bastien Renouil reported on the situation after meeting Olala, highlighting the humanitarian response mobilized to address the case. The development marks a new phase in Kenya's encounter with Ebola and tests the capacity of national response to a border-crossing health threat.

article.articleHeadline: 4,205 Dead in Outbreak; Trump Admin Broke Federal Law; Viola Davis' Shingles
article.articleSummary: As of 9 October 2026, Congo reports 8,728 Ebola cases and 4,205 deaths in an outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus, per WHO. In the United States, a massive cyclosporiasis outbreak causing diarrhea has eroded public confidence in food safety (Gallup). Taylor Farms will halt iceberg lettuce production in Mexico during CDC’s defined cyclosporiasis season from May through the end of August. Walgreens data show purchases of cold and flu medicines up over 20% from last year. A GAO report says the Trump administration withheld Congress-appropriated AHRQ grant funding; a Commonwealth Fund survey flags Medicare affordability concerns. Actress Viola Davis discusses her bout with shingles. WHO unveils a roadmap to tackle hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and new guidance to reduce reliance on institutionalizing people with mental illness. The United States and Zambia sign a $2.49B health-financing deal after removing specimen-sharing and patient-data clauses.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in North Kivu: The Anglican Church Calls on the Faithful to.

The archbishop highlighted church-led awareness and training campaigns and the establishment of care facilities as part of the response, while warning against denial or trivialization that could increase risk. He called on congregants to cooperate with health authorities and adhere to prevention measures to contribute to epidemic control.

article.articleHeadline: DRC: Combating malaria - Advocacy by Impact Santé Afrique and COPEMA-RDC secures the Minister of Health's commitment.
article.articleSummary: Malaria in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) remains a major public health burden, with about 26 million cases and nearly 30,000 deaths in 2025 per the PNLP annual report. Advocacy by Impact Santé Afrique (ISA), COPEMA-RDC, CS4ME, and civil society secured a commitment from Health Minister Samuel Kamba Mulamba to personally monitor PNLP funding and prevent budget cuts. On October 2, 2026, a delegation led by MP Dieudonné Mposhi Kibambi pressed three concrete asks: unlock PNLP operating funds in Q3 2026; ensure PNLP needs are included in the 2027 Finance Law; and strengthen domestic resource mobilization as external funding declines.Internally, the FPS and mandatory health insurance are mobilized to cover simple malaria cases, supported by MoUs with the U.S. government and the Global Fund to bolster response. Civil society will monitor implementation and budget votes to turn commitments into on-ground action in health centers across the country.

article.articleHeadline: Prevalence, characteristics, and clinical course of mpox-related ophthalmic disease (MBOTE-EYE): a prospective cohort study in South Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo
article.articleSummary: MBOTE-EYE is a prospective cohort study conducted in South Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, examining mpox-related ophthalmic disease. It aims to determine the prevalence of ophthalmic involvement among mpox cases, describe clinical characteristics and progression, and monitor outcomes over time. The multicenter cohort collects demographic and clinical data, infection timing, and treatment, with potential laboratory confirmation as reported. By tracking onset to resolution or deterioration, the study provides insights into symptoms such as conjunctival involvement and visual sequelae, informing clinical management of mpox patients. The research brings together institutions across Bukavu, Kinshasa, Goma, and international partners in Belgium, the United States, Canada, France, South Africa, Japan, and beyond, contributing to public health surveillance and response in the DRC as of publication date 2026-10-09.

article.articleHeadline: Cholera, Pipes and Evidence: Doing Rigorous Water Research Inside a Complex
article.articleSummary: In South Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, a cholera-endemic urban water program underscores the need for rigorous, embedded operational research. Climate-driven shocks—floods, droughts, erratic rainfall—heighten unsafe water and diarrhoeal disease, making investments urgent but insufficient without efficient use of funds. Rather than separate research, authors embed evaluation within a large-scale infrastructure upgrade aimed at hundreds of thousands of residents, aligning questions with managers' decisions on prioritisation, affordable connections, and measurement of water quality and cholera incidence. They acknowledge formidable challenges: laboratory capacity and cold chains for water testing; strained surveillance; long project timelines versus short funding cycles; insecure settings and shifting neighbourhoods. Using mixed-methods—quantitative water quality, epidemiology, and qualitative insights from households and institutions—the team shows how multi-stakeholder partnerships can yield practical, policy-relevant evidence on reducing cholera risk and improving water at the point of use.

article.articleHeadline: Case of Suspected Bubonic Plague Outbreak in Russia Could Become a Minor Pandemic
article.articleSummary: Suspected bubonic plague case in Russia could become a minor pandemic, says Prof. Iwan Ariawan of the University of Indonesia’s Public Health Faculty. The expert notes the pathogen is not new, antibiotics are effective, incubation is 1–3 days, and the disease can be severe, aiding rapid detection; transmission requires close contact, and existing lab containment steps appear to limit spread to the laboratory setting. Indonesia’s Health Ministry has upped vigilance for potential spread of the pneumonia‑like illness of unknown origin linked to the event. Enhanced surveillance is being implemented at international entry points, including Bali, with measures such as the Digital Health Declaration (All Indonesia – SSHP) to monitor travel and health, Risk Based Assessment for inbound transport, direct symptom observation (fever, cough, shortness of breath), and vector surveillance for rats and fleas at entry points to curb zoonotic transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Understanding the Symptoms of the Plague, Its Causes, and How It Is Treated.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-09, plague (Yersinia pestis) remains present beyond history, including Indonesia, where rodent and flea populations are high. Transmission occurs mainly via infected flea bites to humans, through contact with infected animal tissue, or via droplets from a pneumonic case. Three forms are described: Bubonic plague, characterized by painful lymph node swelling (bubo) and sudden fever; Septicemic plague, with fever, marked weakness, abdominal symptoms, bleeding under the skin, and possible tissue necrosis; and Pneumonic plague, the most dangerous and the only form transmissible person-to-person through air, causing rapid onset of severe cough with possible hemoptysis, chest pain, high fever, and respiratory failure if untreated within 24 hours. Diagnosis relies on blood, sputum, or lymph node fluid testing. Treatment requires strong antibiotics (streptomycin, gentamicin, or doxycycline) under medical supervision. Prevention emphasizes rodent control and environmental hygiene; seek medical care for high fever and lymph node pain.

The measure calls for government-community collaboration; no case counts, lab confirmations, or infection sources are reported. It emphasizes preparedness and public awareness to curb morbidity linked to poor air quality.

article.articleHeadline: Dangerous disease spreading in Europe - warning to holidaymakers.
article.articleSummary: Autumn holiday travel faces multiple infectious disease threats in Europe, per ECDC and Suomen Rokotepalvelu. Measles outbreaks are seen across Europe, including 40 cases tied to Sweden’s Urkult festival as of 9 September; 28 festival and 12 secondary infections, plus one travel-related case in Finland on a cruise. EU/EEA measles totals for Aug 2025–Jul 2026 are 2,339, with clusters in Bulgaria, Italy, Spain, and France. Outside Europe, outbreaks occur in the United States, Mexico, and Asia (Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines). West Nile virus infections in Europe reached 1,765 by late September, concentrated in Italy, Greece, and Spain; symptoms include fever, headache and myalgia, with rare brain inflammation; higher risk for elderly and immunocompromised. Asia also faces dengue, chikungunya and malaria during the rainy season; Thailand reports 21,620 dengue cases and 31 deaths by end-August. Check travel vaccines and disease status before travel, says Anu Munkki.

article.articleHeadline: Fractional optimal control of hantavirus transmission between rodents and humans
article.articleSummary: Hantavirus transmission between rodents and humans is studied via fractional-order optimal control using Caputo derivatives to capture memory effects in rodent dynamics, environmental contamination, and host recovery. Hantavirus is a serious zoonosis transmitted mainly through inhalation of aerosolized particles from infected rodents; strains include hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. Human-to-human transmission has been reported in specific outbreaks. Rodents are the primary reservoirs; ecological conditions, climate fluctuations, rodent migration, and habitat changes influence persistence and transmission; Asia and South America show increasing prevalence, with Indonesia hosting infected rodent reservoirs in several provinces. Classical ordinary differential equation models offer qualitative insights, but fractional-order models better capture long-memory effects. Fractional optimal control marries memory-aware dynamics with intervention strategies to minimize costs, integrating rodent reduction, environmental sanitation, and treatment controls. The framework reflects broader applications in epidemic systems, and Caputo-based models have been developed for other diseases, such as foot-and-mouth disease.

article.articleHeadline: BKHIT Maluku monitors Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex in cattle in Central Maluku Regency to prevent livestock diseases.
article.articleSummary: As of 9 October 2026, Maluku's Animal, Fish and Plant Quarantine Agency (BKHIT Maluku) is monitoring the Mycobacterium tuberculosis Complex (MTBC) in cattle in Kobisadar District, Central Maluku Regency, to detect bovine tuberculosis risk and prevent zoonotic transmission to humans. Twenty-five cattle will be tested with the tuberculin skin test, involving intradermal tuberculin injection and a 72-hour observation. MTBC includes pathogens such as Mycobacterium bovis, which can affect cattle and people, impacting livestock health, productivity, and food safety. The activity is part of the 2026 HPHK (Hama dan Penyakit Hewan Karantina) monitoring program to map disease status, incidence, and distribution, guiding quarantine controls and animal-health measures under a One Health approach. Results will inform risk assessment, surveillance planning, and sustaining Maluku’s livestock sector and food security.

article.articleHeadline: Study Reveals Malaria and Dengue Fever Cases Are Influenced by Climate Change: What’s the Connection?
article.articleSummary: Monash University researchers report that climate change, via warmer temperatures and altered rainfall, can influence malaria and dengue fever transmission by expanding suitable habitats for Anopheles and Aedes mosquitoes, though effects are non-linear and vary by season and location. The study, published in Science Advances, emphasizes that vector control, urbanization, and housing conditions also shape risk. In Indonesia, malaria cases rose from about 418,000 in 2023 to 706,000 in 2025, while dengue fever affected about 161,937 people in 2025 (57.02 per 100,000). Researchers, including Dr. Toby Cumming and Associate Professor Henry Surendra, collaborated with Indonesia’s Ministry of Health in Kalimantan Timur to identify climate, environmental, and demographic drivers. Prevention strategies call for an integrated approach beyond climate, including vector control and health interventions. The World Mosquito Program’s Wolbachia-infected Aedes releases aim to reduce dengue transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Fatty Liver Cells Turn On a Caspase-2 Death Pathway That Damps Hepatitis B
article.articleSummary: HBV infection intersects with MASLD; in vitro study from China uses HepG2.2.15 HBV-producing hepatocytes from Central South University’s Second Xiangya Hospital. Free fatty acids (oleate:palmitate 2:1) induce steatosis, confirmed by triglyceride content and Oil Red O staining. Lipotoxicity triggers a modest apoptosis and activates a TNF-α/TNFR1/Caspase-8/Caspase-2 axis. All HBV replication markers decline concurrently: intracellular HBV DNA, pregenomic RNA, HBsAg, and HBeAg. TNF-α neutralization partially restores viral markers and reduces pathway activation, providing causal evidence that this inflammatory signaling suppresses HBV under lipotoxic stress. The study further uses a Caspase-2 inhibitor to probe its role, implying Caspase-2 contributes to reduced HBV replication in steatotic cells.

article.articleHeadline: Autumn seafood marketed in bulk; beware of foodborne diseases.
article.articleSummary: Autumn seafood markets in Nanchang reopen after the summer fishing moratorium, with abundant fish, shrimp, crabs, and shellfish. The Nanchang Center for Disease Control issues a health alert warning that seafood can trigger gastroenteritis, allergic reactions, and gout if misused. Key recommendations: verify freshness (fish eyes bright, gills red, flesh firm; crabs lively with intact shells; prawns translucent; shellfish that close and spit sand); avoid raw or undercooked seafood to prevent parasites and Vibrio parahaemolyticus. Prefer quick cooking methods (steaming or brief boiling) to preserve flavor; store seafood promptly in refrigeration or freezing; do not keep at room temperature. Moderate consumption and consideration of personal health are advised; those with cold-prone stomachs or diarrhea risk should limit high-purine items like crabs and shellfish, and avoid pairing with icy drinks or raw fruit. Buy from reputable supermarkets or farmers markets to ensure safety.

article.articleHeadline: ScienceNet: New progress in research on the transmission risk of pangolin-origin antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
article.articleSummary: 5 of 22 fecal isolates from pangolins rescued in 2018 (Malayan pangolins, Manis javanica) carried multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli, spanning sequence types ST354, ST206, and ST48. Core resistances include beta-lactams, chloramphenicol, fluoroquinolones, and sulfonamides, with resistance genes co-located on IncX1 plasmids. Plasmids harbor abundant mobile elements—class 1 integrons, IS26, and transposon Tn1721—that promote horizontal gene transfer. Conjugation experiments demonstrated efficient transfer of resistance plasmids to recipient E. coli, enabling rapid acquisition of multidrug resistance. Phylogenomic and comparative genomics show these MDR E. coli are closely related to human and animal isolates from East Asia and Southeast Asia, with some resistance plasmids highly homologous to globally reported plasmids, suggesting pangolins could facilitate cross-ecological spread of resistance. While virulence of the isolates was overall low, dissemination of resistance genes poses public health risks. Wildlife trade contributes to cross-border AMR spread; supports enhanced wildlife quarantine and One Health antimicrobial resistance controls. Published in Integrative Zoology (doi:10.1111/1749-4877.70161) on 2026-10-09.

article.articleHeadline: Rare Black Yeast Fungus Linked to Lung Inflammation in Landmark Case Report
article.articleSummary: China-based case from Hangzhou (Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine) reports a 45-year-old man with three weeks of chest tightness and exertional dyspnea. CT revealed diffuse bilateral pulmonary nodules. BAL with targeted next-generation sequencing initially detected Streptococcus pneumoniae, but antibiotics failed and disease progressed. Transbronchial lung cryobiopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with negative fungal/mycobacterial staining. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing on BAL identified Exophiala oligosperma, a melanized black yeast, with 88 reads and an RPTM of 34 per 10 million, confirming pulmonary phaeohyphomycosis. Exophiala oligosperma is rare in lungs but commonly originates from wet environments (shower drains, sink traps), making exposure plausible. Open-access report in BMC Infectious Diseases highlights the diagnostic value of mNGS in atypical granulomatous lung disease, underscoring the need to distinguish true pathogens from bystander colonization.

article.articleHeadline: A study reveals that 12 percent of cancer cases are triggered by preventable infections.
article.articleSummary: As of 2024, a global analysis published in The Lancet Oncology by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) finds that about 2.3 million new cancer cases—roughly 1 in 8 worldwide—are directly linked to infection. Of 37 infection–cancer pairs studied, two pathogens dominate: Helicobacter pylori, a stomach bacterium, associated with about 760,000 gastric cancer cases; and Human Papillomavirus (HPV), responsible for about 750,000 cancers, including nearly all cervical cancers (~600,000) and additional oropharyngeal, anal, and penile cancers. Other infectious drivers include hepatitis B and C (liver cancer), Epstein–Barr virus, and HIV. The heaviest burden appears in East Asia and in low- to middle-income countries. Prevention potential is substantial: HPV and hepatitis B vaccines; routine screening (Pap smear, HPV testing, hepatitis B/C testing); and early eradication of H. pylori with antibiotics. Healthcare interventions could substantially reduce future cancer incidence.

article.articleHeadline: Sea fish carry "flesh-eating bacteria"; Shenzhen man nearly died after being stabbed as his palm rotted and fever persisted.
article.articleSummary: On 9 October 2026, a Shenzhen seafood seller sustained a right-palmar puncture from a fish spine, then developed sepsis from Vibrio vulnificus (ocean wound pathogen) after neglecting wound care. Within hours he had fever (39°C), swelling, chills, and body aches. Laboratory tests showed leukocytosis, neutrophilia, and elevated procalcitonin; blood cultures confirmed Vibrio vulnificus infection. He underwent antimicrobial therapy and local wound care during a 7-day hospital stay, then transferred to Shenzhen Third People's Hospital due to persistent infection. MRI found a 2 cm forearm abscess; with precise antimicrobial therapy and wound management, swelling and pain subsided and infection markers normalized. He was discharged with outpatient follow-up. Vibrio vulnificus is a high-mortality flesh-eating bacterium in warm coastal waters and seafood; untreated mortality 50-70%, approaching 100% within 72 hours. Prevention: wear gloves when handling seafood; wash and disinfect wounds; ensure seafood is cooked; avoid seawater contact with wounds.

article.articleHeadline: Pneumonic Plague in Russia: A Psychic Prophecy About the Pandemic.
article.articleSummary: On 9 October 2026, media report a British clairvoyant’s warning of a possible new bacterial pandemic tied to pneumonic plague in Russia. Briton Kreigs Hamiltons-Pārkers claimed that on 24 September two Tibetan monks visited his home and spoke of a forthcoming outbreak distinct from prior ones. A 28-year-old Darja Shipilova, who worked at Irkutsk’s institute, died in Siberia; provisional data suggest she may have contracted pneumonic plague, a severe lung infection capable of rapid progression. There is no proven link between the clairvoyant’s statements and Shipilova’s death. Hamiltons-Pārkers has previously attracted attention for predicting COVID-19, and now asserts monks knew medicines for the upcoming disease, with AI potentially aiding treatment development. The article notes no scientific validation for his forecasts and remains cautious about implied causes or outbreak scope.

article.articleHeadline: When your child develops a cough and fever, don’t tough it out! Be vigilant for respiratory syncytial virus infection | Health Science Column
article.articleSummary: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in children is highlighted as a common autumn–winter threat in China, with infants under 6 months at highest risk for severe disease, particularly those who are preterm or have congenital heart disease, chronic lung disease, or immune deficiencies. Early RSV symptoms resemble a cold—nasal congestion, runny nose, mild fever, and reduced appetite—but after about two days cough can worsen with wheeze and increased work of breathing; very young infants may not have fever and may present with poor feeding or irritability. Hospitalization is advised for rapid or labored breathing, significant feeding reduction, decreased urine output, or lethargy; for infants under 3 months with fever, urgent care is recommended. Home care includes ensuring ventilation and appropriate humidity, small frequent feeds to prevent dehydration, avoiding tremella soup and Chuanbei powder, avoiding dairy and cold foods, nasal suction, and not using antibiotics. Prevention emphasizes hand hygiene, ventilation, masking when someone is ill, limiting exposure of high-risk infants, and physician-guided immunoprophylaxis. Originates from Chengdu-based pediatric specialists in Sichuan, China.

article.articleHeadline: Plague as a Biological Weapon. Unit 731, Ningbo, and the Siege of Kaffa | HISTORIA.org.pl
article.articleSummary: On October 27, 1940, Japanese aircraft dropped fleas infected with Yersinia pestis over Ningbo, Zhejiang, China, triggering a plague outbreak; the first death occurred on October 30. By November 2 authorities sealed the outbreak area, and on November 3 plague was confirmed. The attack aimed to provoke epidemics and fear, leveraging advanced knowledge of transmission. It was part of Shirō Ishii’s Unit 731 bioweapons program, tied to a broader network including 1644 in Nanjing and Unit 100 in Changchun. In Ningbo, isolation teams, decontamination, and burials were organized; seven households reported no survivors. Unit 731 conducted deadly experiments on prisoners—deliberately infecting them with plague, cholera, and anthrax, sometimes via vivisection. Some estimates suggest up to 600 prisoners were killed annually at a single facility during such experiments.

article.articleHeadline: Possible norovirus in raspberry pastries sold at nine Montreal-area bakeries
article.articleSummary: Norovirus contamination risk tied to Alasko-brand frozen raspberries from China triggered a Canadian Food Inspection Agency recall and a MAPAQ warning about raspberry pastries sold at Boulangerie Ange in Montreal-area suburbs. Affected products are raspberry tart, raspberry tartlet, and, at some locations, raspberry Danish, sold individually between Sept. 8–11 at nine Boulangerie Ange sites (some packaged with a Boulangerie Ange label); pastries may also have been sold online or through community groups. The ministry notes a few illness cases have been reported to MAPAQ linked to the recalled raspberries. Symptoms of norovirus include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal cramps, typically starting 24–48 hours after exposure. Consumers are advised not to eat these pastries and to seek medical care if symptoms develop. MAPAQ is reviewing other Quebec retailers; more recalls could follow. For questions: smsaia@mapaq.gouv.qc.ca.

article.articleHeadline: Syphilis Bacteria Found in Spinal Fluid Across All Disease Stages
article.articleSummary: In a Shanghai, China-based study published in BMC Infectious Diseases, Treponema pallidum DNA was detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of HIV-negative adults across all syphilis stages, including early primary/secondary, latent, and symptomatic neurosyphilis. The Tongji University-affiliated Shanghai Skin Disease Hospital enrolled 155 untreated patients (47 primary/secondary, 70 latent, 38 neurosyphilis). CSF and blood plasma were analyzed by nested PCR targeting polA and Tpp47. Detection in CSF occurred in 17.0% of primary/secondary, 17.1% latent, and 28.9% neurosyphilis (P=0.284). Roughly one in six early/latent cases, and nearly one in three symptomatic cases, carried CSF DNA; importantly, 14.6% with normal TPPA/RPR and normal CSF still harbored bacterial DNA. CSF–plasma agreement was poor (kappa 0.1). Findings imply CNS invasion can occur early and silently, challenging reliance on standard CSF markers.

article.articleHeadline: Low Sodium and High Neutrophils Mark Severe COVID-19 in Children, Study
article.articleSummary: In a retrospective Chinese study of 519 children hospitalized with symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection (Dec 2022–Dec 2025), 345 (66.4%) were infants or toddlers. Disease severity split: 37.0% mild (192), 43.7% moderate (227), 19.3% severe/critical (100); all patients recovered. Compared BA.5-dominant period with post-BA.5 period, severe/critical disease, supplemental oxygen use, length of stay, and complications were significantly higher during BA.5 era. Neurological symptoms were more frequent in the BA.5 period, while viral co-detection was lower. Multivariable analysis initially flagged neurological symptoms, BA.5 period, and young age as risk factors for severe/critical disease, but sensitivity analyses using Firth penalized regression showed Definitional circularity and unstable age/period effects. Only hyponatremia (low sodium) and elevated neutrophil count remained robust predictors across analyses, suggesting two simple laboratory measures may reliably signal impending severity in pediatric COVID-19.

article.articleHeadline: India struggles to curb leprosy transmission
article.articleSummary: India reported 91,783 new leprosy cases in 2025-26, 41.2% above the projected 65,000, with child cases 91.6% above projection. Grade 2 Disability (G2D) among new cases was 1.34 per million, above the target of 1 per million. National prevalence stood at 0.56 per 10,000 at end-March 2026, below the elimination threshold of <1 per 10,000, but transmission remains geographically concentrated: states with highest prevalence were Chhattisgarh (1.66), Jharkhand (1.51), Chandigarh (1.49), Odisha (1.25), and Maharashtra (1.14) per 10,000. District-level burden: 14.8% of districts (>1/10,000) in 2025-26, down from 18.6% in 2013-14; 114 districts above elimination target, while only 148 districts achieved interruption of transmission (vs 300 projected). G2D cases (1,945 total) clustered in Chandigarh, Delhi, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha (42.5%). Chandigarh 13.54, Delhi 11.53, Chhattisgarh 7.87 per million. SDR PEP coverage reached 91.2% of 16.94 lakh eligible contacts in 2025-26 (up from 71.4% of 6.48 lakh in 2019-20). Source: National Leprosy Eradication Programme (2025-26).

article.articleHeadline: Innovation. A novel green light-activated tech to fight bacterial infections
article.articleSummary: Os(II) metallophotoantibiotics Os1–Os3, activated by green light, inhibit bacterial growth and disrupt biofilms, addressing antimicrobial resistance and infected wound healing. IIT (BHU) Varanasi researchers Banerjee and Mukherjee tested against Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus subtilis, with Os1 showing the strongest antibacterial activity. Green-light activation generates reactive oxygen species that damage bacterial cells and interfere with essential processes, enabling substantial biofilm suppression. In rat infection models, Os1 achieved approximately 85% inhibition of biofilm formation in E. coli and Bacillus subtilis. The study, published in Communications Chemistry (Nature Portfolio), underscores IIT (BHU)’s interdisciplinary collaboration across chemistry, biomedical engineering, and pharmaceutical engineering and points to potential therapeutic development for device-associated infections.

article.articleHeadline: With dengue surging, experts push for QDENGA vaccine access, private
article.articleSummary: Bangladesh faces a worsening dengue surge with 90,356 hospitalisations and 294 deaths this year, alongside 1,935 new admissions. Health experts urge government approval of WHO-prequalified QDENGA (TAK-003) dengue vaccine to reduce severe cases, hospitalisations and fatalities, arguing private imports could extend access while national rollout is being decided. QDENGA is a two-dose vaccine given three months apart, and WHO recommends it for children aged 6–16 in high-transmission settings; it provides protection against all four dengue serotypes. In Bangladesh, officials stress that vaccine evaluation should be evidence-based and not rushed, since immediate impact is unlikely. Globally, QDENGA has WHO prequalification (May 2024), SAGE endorsement (Sept 2023), and has been approved in 43 countries; India approved on 20 July 2026, planning commercial launch in early 2027 with price Rs 6,000–12,000. Safety notes prohibit vaccination for pregnant women, under-six children, and some immunocompromised individuals. Private import could ease access and hospital burden.

article.articleHeadline: Symptoms of Lumpy Skin Disease in cows and buffaloes, take these steps immediately.
article.articleSummary: Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD) is spreading again among dairy cattle, especially cows and buffaloes, across several Indian states as of October 9, 2026. The infection causes fever, and round, painful nodules appearing on the neck, muzzle, back and legs; excessive watery or thick saliva from mouth and nose; marked lethargy; sudden drop in milk yield; and in some cases difficulty standing due to leg swelling. Immediate actions include isolating symptomatic animals from healthy herd, housing them in ventilated shelters, using separate drinking troughs, and sanitizing handlers and clothing. Transmission is mainly vector-borne via flies, mosquitoes, ticks and wasps, with water stagnation around sheds facilitating spread. Control measures include eliminating stagnant water, fumigating with camphor or dried neem leaves, and targeted disinfectant spraying. There is no cure; treatment is symptomatic. Do not use heavy antibiotics; consult government veterinary hospital. Vaccination with goatpox or LSD-ProVac vaccines is advised to prevent further spread.

article.articleHeadline: One human protein helps malaria and kala-azar thrive. JNU scientists took it out
article.articleSummary: JNU researchers in Delhi report that removing a human protein, p38-MAPK, undermines both malaria parasites (Plasmodium) and kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) in lab systems. The study, published June 11 in Communications Biology, used PROTAC NR-7h to selectively degrade p38-MAPK in human macrophages and red blood cells, leaving ERK1/2 intact. In infected cells, NR-7h reduced kala-azar parasite levels up to ~16-fold and malaria parasite burden similarly, without harming host cells; parasites grown alone were unaffected. Removing the protein disrupted immune signaling, with TNF-alpha and IL-12 responses altered. Timing matters: p38-MAPK activity rose around six hours post-infection and declined by twelve hours, suggesting early defense but later parasite support. Malaria caused ~610,000 deaths and 282 million cases in 2024 worldwide; kala-azar affects India (Bihar, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand) with 50,000–90,000 new cases annually; drug resistance reported in eight African countries. No animal or human trials yet; host-directed therapy.

article.articleHeadline: Gadchiroli Malaria Control | Malaria control in Gadchiroli; positivity rate at 0.32 percent.
article.articleSummary: As of 9 October 2026, Gadchiroli district in Maharashtra reports notable malaria control gains. Malaria positivity dropped from 0.49% (Jan–Sep 2025) to 0.32% (Jan–Sep 2026), and cases declined from 6,411 to 3,940. From January to September 2026, 1,219,783 malaria tests were performed: 507,675 blood smear microscopy and 712,108 rapid diagnostic tests. The annual parasite index fell from 6.42 to 4.62. Up to July 2026, six malaria deaths occurred; August–September recorded zero malaria deaths. Vector control included indoor residual spraying in 1,195 villages covering 160,956 households, and 116,372 insecticide-treated nets distributed. In 150 ashram schools, 39,663 students were screened; 371 infected and 566 treated, with total compensation of Rs 283,000 paid to treated students. Gadchiroli ranks first nationwide in NITI Aayog Delta Ranking. Two girls went missing from a Maseli ashram school; investigations ongoing. Citizens are urged to use bed nets, avoid standing water, and seek prompt testing for fever.

article.articleHeadline: Stringent measures to control infectious diseases
article.articleSummary: On 2026-10-09, in Madikeri, District Collector S. J. Someshankar chaired the District Surveillance Committee and outlined measures to curb infectious diseases in Kodagu, including dengue, malaria, vector-borne illnesses, dog-bite (rabies) cases, biomedical waste management, hospital infection control, tobacco control, HIV prevention, and HPV vaccination progress. District Health Officer Dr. Satish Kumar said 2,502 febrile samples were tested, with 42 dengue cases confirmed; monsoon activities include house-to-house surveys, larval source reduction, and public awareness. Dog-bite cases up to Sept 2026 total 999; ensure timely anti-rabies vaccination and immunoglobulin supply. The meeting reviewed sanitation, waste disposal, and adherence to national health service standards. Under the National Tobacco Control Programme, 64 raids yielded Rs 109,700 in fines. HPV vaccination as of Aug 6: 70.79% of 5,256 targets (3,735 vaccinated); Somwarpet taluk leads at 74.88%. Kodagu aims to become a Safe+ district by year-end 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Demand to declare some parts of Madhya Pradesh's districts as epidemic-affected areas after the deaths of 35 tribal children; Supreme Court has sought a response.
article.articleSummary: Measles and rubella outbreak amid severe malnutrition has spurred a Public Interest Litigation in the Supreme Court of India seeking to declare Birsa and Bahar blocks in Balaghat district, Madhya Pradesh, as epidemic-affected under the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897. The plea — Ajab Lal Lilhare v. Union of India — cites over 35 deaths among Baiga and other PVTG children, attributed to measles-rubella and acute malnutrition. It alleges administrative negligence, inadequate health facilities, and failure to vaccinate on time, demanding compensation for affected families, safe drinking water, nutritious food, and rapid welfare scheme implementation. The Supreme Court bench of Chief Justice Suryakant and Justices Joymaly Bagchi and V. Mohana has issued notices to the Centre, state government, NHRC, and others. Authorities reportedly faced written warnings in January 2026, yet delays persisted in monitoring and response."

triage.headline_ja: 35人の部族の子供の死亡を受け、マディヤ・プラデーシュ州の一部地域を感染症流行地域に指定するよう求める請願；最高裁判所が回答を求める
triage.triage_reason: 麻疹・風疹の流行により35人の部族children（PVTG）が死亡し、最高裁が中央・州政府等に通知を発出するなど公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と政治的関心の高まりが確認されるため。
triage.notes: 発生地域はインド・マディヤ・プラデーシュ州バラガート県の特定ブロック（Birsa, Bahar）に限定される局地的事例。国際的拡大や渡航制限の兆候は記事からは確認できない。栄養失調と予防接種の遅れが背景にあり、脆弱な先住民コミュニティ（Baiga等PVTG）に集中している点が特徴的。

article.articleHeadline: Low Platelet Count In Dengue? 7 Foods And Care Tips To Support Platelet Recovery Naturally
article.articleSummary: Delhi reports 695 dengue cases in 2026; the first week of October saw 98 new cases. Dengue is transmitted by Aedes aegypti. Common symptoms include headache, retro-orbital pain, and muscle or joint pain. Platelet counts can fall during dengue and may not require transfusion; regular blood tests and clinical monitoring guide treatment. Hydration is essential; fluids such as coconut water, ORS, and lemon water help, and fresh juices (papaya, pomegranate, kiwi) may aid fluids and nutrients but do not cure dengue. Papaya leaf juice is sometimes recommended, but evidence is limited and it should not replace medical care. There is no specific antiviral; treatment is supportive and based on symptoms. Avoid self-medication; avoid aspirin and ibuprofen unless advised. Seek urgent medical evaluation for warning signs, especially around defervescence, as dengue can progress to severe illness.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱による血小板減少？血小板回復を自然にサポートする7つの食品とケアのコツ

article.articleHeadline: Gurugram dengue tally rises to 70 with 2 fresh cases, Haryana tally crosses 500
article.articleSummary: Two new dengue cases in Gurugram lift the district's dengue tally to 70, surpassing 64 cases recorded in all of 2025. Haryana state reports 503 dengue cases by October 4, up from 318 on September 14 (≈58% rise in 20 days). Gurugram previously had the state's highest tally with 65; updated district bulletin now lists 70, five more than earlier this week; statewide total not provided in Friday bulletin. A total of 13,797 samples have been tested in Gurugram to date, with 137 tested on Friday; no dengue-related deaths confirmed in the district this year. Rapid fever survey teams covered 16,642 houses on Friday, bringing annual coverage to 1.524 million homes; 7,935 notices under Section 214 for mosquito-control have been issued. Dengue is linked to mosquito breeding after the monsoon; residents advised to prevent water accumulation in coolers, pots, rooftop containers, and other areas. Gurugram reported five malaria cases so far this year; no new malaria on Friday.

triage.headline_ja: グルガオンのデング熱累計が70例に増加、ハリヤナ州の累計は500例を突破
triage.triage_reason: 季節性デング熱の増加だが、死亡例なく通常の季節的流行の範囲内であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低い。ただし増加率が高いため経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 地元メディアによる季節的なデング熱・マラリアの発生状況報告。死亡例なく、地方自治体による対策（蚊対策の通知発行、家屋調査）が進行中で管理可能な状況と見られる。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue cases surge in Pune as Oct heat boost mosquito breeding
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever surges in Pune, India, as October heat and lingering humidity boost Aedes breeding. Since January, Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) records over 1,700 suspected dengue cases and 90 confirmed across the city; by Oct 8, 96 suspected and 25 confirmed in October. Chikungunya totals stand at 26. Hospitals report rising dengue admissions, with longer recovery and complications such as serositis, dengue hepatitis, dengue shock syndrome, and low platelets, including in children. Experts attribute the uptick to post-monsoon heat, humidity and standing water sustaining transmission, though heat alone is not the cause. Emphasis on early testing and vigilance: monitor fever, hydration, and platelet/hematocrit levels; seek medical care rather than self-medicating. Preventive measures urged: eliminate stagnant water, use repellents, wear covered clothing, and employ nets or screens.

triage.headline_ja: 10月の暑さで蚊の繁殖が増加、プネーでデング熱患者が急増
triage.triage_reason: インドのプネーで季節性のデング熱・チクングニア熱が増加しているが、既知の毎年の流行パターンであり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いため、フルRRAには至らないが経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 毎年のモンスーン後に見られる季節性のデング熱・チクングニア熱の増加。重症化例（デング性肝炎、ショック症候群等）の報告があるが、地域的な公衆衛生対応の範囲内と考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: Relentless malaria; more among disease carriers and migrant workers in Idukki's plantation belt.
article.articleSummary: Malaria remains a challenge in Kerala, with rising transmission among migrant workers in Idukki's plantation belt, despite local control efforts. In 2026, 983 people have been confirmed with malaria and seven deaths, six of which were migrant workers. Most cases cluster among migrant laborers in Idukki, including workers from Jharkhand, Odisha, and Bihar, with hundreds affected. In Ernakulam district, Perumbavoor and Kakkanad report a second concentration, largely linked to workers from Odisha, Bengal, and Bihar. Return of migrants during election periods coincides with higher case counts this year. Malaria is transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes that bite at night. Symptoms include high fever, chills, headache, and weakness; fever with shivering warrants blood testing. Prevention focuses on avoiding bites (bed nets, repellents) and eliminating standing water in ponds, irrigation channels, pits, wells, and water-filled tires.

triage.headline_ja: 執拗なマラリア：イドゥッキのプランテーション地帯で感染者・移民労働者の間で増加
triage.triage_reason: マラリアはケララ州の既知の風土病で、移民労働者間での季節的増加と見られるが、死亡例を伴う中等度の重症度があり、継続的な曝露リスクも示唆されるため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: マラリアはインドの複数州（ジャールカンド、オディシャ、ビハール、ベンガル）出身の移民労働者を中心にケララ州で感染拡大。地域の既知の風土病であり、国際的拡大リスクは低いが、継続的なベクター曝露と死亡例の発生から経過観察が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Flu-like illnesses rise across Kashmir, doctors urge precautions
article.articleSummary: Influenza has an early start in Kashmir this year, with a surge across age groups and areas around Srinagar as winter approaches. Respiratory infections are increasing, and influenza can lead to complications requiring hospitalisation in high‑risk groups. Pulmonologist Prof. Naveed Nazir Shah notes the surge began earlier this year, with September activity rather than November as typical; secondary infections and pneumonia are being observed. Seek medical help if symptoms persist beyond a week, or if breathlessness or high fever occurs. High‑risk individuals—diabetes, lung disease, or immunocompromised—should receive the trivalent influenza vaccine this season; children under five are also advised to vaccinate. SKIMS issued a public health advisory urging influenza and pneumonia vaccination, hand hygiene, and avoidance of unnecessary antibiotics. Autumn/winter conditions favour viral spread and can worsen asthma, COPD, and cardiovascular ailments. Most people recover in about a week, but lab confirmation is needed to prove influenza.

triage.headline_ja: カシミール地方でインフルエンザ様疾患が増加、医師らが注意を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザの早期流行であり、重症例や死亡の報告は明示されていないが、例年より早い時期の流行開始であるため経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 例年より早いインフルエンザ流行（9月から）で、当局（SKIMS）が公衆衛生勧告を発出。重症度・死亡者数などの定量的データは記事に記載なく不明。季節性インフルエンザの範囲内である可能性が高いが、早期発生のパターンのため継続監視が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Fever for two weeks, diagnosis made from a small ulcer.
article.articleSummary: A 54-year-old Cambodian woman presented with two weeks of fever, headache, malaise, cough, abdominal pain, and vomiting, developing dyspnea and chills before admission to Xuyên Á Tay Ninh General Hospital in Tay Ninh, Vietnam. Lab tests showed rising liver enzymes consistent with acute liver injury. Initial workup ruled out viral hepatitis, biliary infection, liver abscess, dengue, malaria, and sepsis. The turning point was a small, dry, crusted eschar on the abdominal skin, with gardening exposure and prolonged fever prompting consideration of scrub typhus; real-time PCR of blood confirmed Orientia tsutsugamushi. She was treated with doxycycline, fever resolved within a day, and health improved over two weeks. Clinicians note scrub typhus has diverse, often misleading presentations and that painless, hidden eschars can be missed. There is currently no vaccine available for scrub typhus.

article.articleHeadline: Urgently Contain the Lumpy Skin Disease Outbreak in Buffalo and Cattle.
article.articleSummary: Lumpy Skin Disease outbreak affecting buffalo and cattle in Tuyen Quang province, Vietnam, prompts intensified vaccination and control measures as of Oct 9, 2026. Nearly 55,000 vaccine doses have been administered in the province; about 17,000 in outbreak-affected communes and 38,000 in non-outbreak areas. Authorities also procure lime powder and chemicals for distribution, reinforce surveillance, rapid sampling, sanitation, and disinfection, and tighten controls on movement, sale, and slaughter of animals to prevent spread. The provincial government has issued directives to raise Autumn-Winter 2026 vaccination coverage to at least 80% of the herd and to conduct mass vaccination in September-October 2026, with commune leaders held accountable. The campaign follows low Spring-Summer vaccination rates and ongoing threats from African swine fever, avian influenza A/H5N1, and other diseases; gaps in immunization risk wider spread, especially under favorable conditions for vectors.

article.articleHeadline: Hong Kong records new imported dengue fever and chikungunya fever cases.
article.articleSummary: Hong Kong reports two imported mosquito-borne cases for Oct 2–8, 2026: dengue fever in a traveler who had been to Vietnam, and chikungunya fever in a 73-year-old man who had travelled to Mainland China. The dengue total in Hong Kong this year is 33 (31 imported, 2 local); last year 2025 had 59 (all imported); 2024 had 161 (156 imported, 5 local). The chikungunya total this year is 5 (4 imported, 1 local); last year 2025 had 82 (11 local). Globally, dengue incidence remains high: last year >90 countries reported >5 million cases and >4,000 deaths; Jan–Aug 2026 ~2.2 million cases and >1,000 deaths. Nearby, Sri Lanka and Vietnam exceed 100,000 cases this year; Bangladesh and Cambodia >80,000; Indonesia and Malaysia >70,000; Singapore >2,600; Guangdong Province, China, by Aug 31 reported 431 dengue cases (August 496). For chikungunya, globally last year 502,264 cases and 186 deaths; Guangdong by Aug 31 reported 739 chikungunya infections (August 496). Public health advice: use mosquito repellents (DEET or equivalent), eliminate standing water, change vase water weekly, keep drains clear, report mosquito problems at 1823.

article.articleHeadline: Viet Nam's Private-Sector TB Bridge Added Thousands of Cases to
article.articleSummary: Vietnam TB program spans 15 provinces with about 40.6 million people and piloted a public-private mix (PPM) bridge 2020–2023 to link 3,154 out-of-network providers to the national TB program. The intervention used active case finding, provider referral incentives, patient support, and near real-time integrated data systems to convert private-sector diagnoses into national notifications. Analyzing 2016–2025 province-quarter data, adjusting for province and calendar-quarter fixed effects and COVID-19 disruptions, the study found an average increase of 316.8 TB notifications per province per quarter (95% CI 23.4–610.2; p=0.034). Nationally, this equates to about 3,206 additional notifications per year (CI 1,658–4,763; p<0.001). Dose–response showed every 100 verbal assessments per 100,000 population linked to a 1.4% rise in notifications (IRR 1.00014; 95% CI 1.00002–1.00025; p=0.018); national models showed a 3.5% increase (IRR 1.00035; p<0.001). Findings support private-sector bridges as scalable, cost-efficient growth in TB case reporting.

article.articleHeadline: Measles has returned: outbreaks of a dangerous disease are being recorded worldwide due to vaccine refusal.
article.articleSummary: Measles has returned worldwide due to vaccine refusal, with rubella and pertussis resurging in Russia where 28% abstain from immunization. Anti-vaccine sentiment is higher among youth, blaming vaccines for harm or promoting pharma-conspiracy memes online. By 2025, vaccination rates fell to a ten-year low, notably for measles, hepatitis A and tuberculosis. In the United States, measles cases approach 4,000, a 35-year high, with two-thirds in children or teens; New York has declared a state of emergency as eradication proclaimed in 2000 fades. Pertussis outbreaks reappear, and reports of plague, Legionella, typhus, and typhoid rise. In Bangladesh, the world’s largest measles outbreak has killed nearly 1,000, with about 80% of cases under 18; infants under 9 months are at highest risk due to vaccination gaps. Indonesia (including Bali), Vietnam, and Thailand also rank among top measles transmitters.

triage.headline_ja: 麻疹が復活：ワクチン拒否により世界各地で危険な疾患の集団発生が記録されている
triage.triage_reason: 複数国（インドネシア、ベトナム、タイを含む）で麻疹を中心としたワクチン予防可能疾患の国際的な再流行が報告され、米国では35年ぶりの高水準、ニューヨーク州が緊急事態を宣言するなど、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も高い。

article.articleHeadline: Russia's rodent-borne outbreak status is unclear; scholars urge suspending air travel to these two countries to prevent the outbreak from spreading.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-09, Russia reports an unclear pneumonic plague outbreak; public health officials urge swift action to prevent international spread. Drawing on COVID-19 lessons, Brookings senior fellow argues Western nations should not trust statements from authoritarian regimes and should proactively suspend air travel to outbreak regions. The immediate focus targets tourist destinations heavily frequented by Russian travelers: Turkey and Thailand. 2025 estimates indicate nearly 7 million Russian tourists to Turkey and about 2 million to Thailand, making these two countries the most likely sources if pneumonic plague spreads abroad. Other destinations cited include Italy, South Korea, Japan, Germany, the United States, Singapore, Cyprus, Finland, and Vietnam, but with less emphasis. The article stresses halting flights to Turkey and Thailand to curb cross-border dissemination, rather than waiting for full confirmation of cases.

triage.triage_reason: ロシアで肺ペストの発生状況が不明確なまま国際的拡大への懸念が提起され、専門家が渡航制限（航空便停止）を提言しており、IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大リスク・渡航制限）に該当するためフルRRAへの移行が妥当。ただし対象国リストに含まれる具体的発生国は確認されない。

article.articleHeadline: Side, Turkey: Five-star hotel plagued by mass infections
article.articleSummary: As of 9 October 2026, the five-star Bosphorus Sorgun hotel in Side, Turkey, faces a mass outbreak of intestinal infections, with dozens of tourists—many from Russia—reporting vomiting and diarrhea. Guests cite poor sanitary conditions, including low-quality water and hygiene lapses (staff at a beach bar rinsing glasses with water instead of washing). The outbreak involves guests from multiple countries; similar incidents were reported at the same hotel in August and September this year. No laboratory-confirmed pathogen or case count is provided. The report also notes other traveler health concerns, such as a Russian tourist from Lyubertsy hospitalized after dengue fever diagnosed in Vietnam, believed mosquito-bite–transmitted during sleep.

triage.triage_reason: トルコの一ホテルでの胃腸炎様集団感染（病原体未特定）であり、同ホテルで8月・9月にも同様の事案が繰り返されているため経過観察とするが、重症度・国際的拡大のエビデンスは乏しい。付随して言及されたベトナムでのデング熱は渡航者の輸入例単発であり、現地流行を示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 疾患タグは'Dengue'だが、記事の主題はトルコの一ホテルでの胃腸炎様集団感染（病原体未確認）。ベトナムでのデング熱言及は、ロシア人旅行者1名の輸入症例であり、ベトナム国内での流行拡大を示す情報は含まれていないため、対象国としては計上しない。トルコ・ロシアはいずれも対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: Heat Erodes Wolbachia Shield Against Dengue in Mosquitoes, Study Finds
article.articleSummary: Vietnamese laboratory study shows elevated rearing temperature weakens Wolbachia (wMel)-mediated protection against dengue virus (DENV) in Aedes aegypti. Using blood from thirteen dengue patients at Ho Chi Minh City’s Hospital for Tropical Diseases to feed wMel-infected mosquitoes, researchers compared cohorts raised at 28±4°C and 31±4°C. At 31°C, infectious saliva appeared more frequently, signaling greater potential for human transmission; nevertheless, the Wolbachia block was not abolished, as wMel-infected mosquitoes remained less likely than wild-type to produce infectious saliva. Heat reduced Wolbachia densities in ovaries, midgut, and salivary glands, plausibly explaining reduced blocking. Dengue serotypes DENV-1 and DENV-4 replicated more at higher temperatures in wMel mosquitoes. Dissemination to head/thorax and viral load in those tissues predicted breakthrough infections, whereas Wolbachia density did not. Implications: wMel deployments remain valuable but efficacy margins narrow during hot conditions linked to urban heat islands and climate change in dengue-endemic regions.

article.articleHeadline: Nationwide Survey of Cambodian Bats Reveals Hidden Diversity of Malaria
article.articleSummary: Cambodia-wide bat survey uncovers 13% carriage of haemosporidian parasites across 1,180 individuals from 34 species (CamBatRat, 2016–2020). Two genera dominate: Polychromophilus (bat-restricted) and Hepatocystis (related to Plasmodium). Infections were confirmed by multilocus sequencing (cytb, cox1, clpC, ef2, pat) from 152 bats across four families: Emballonuridae, Hipposideridae, Pteropodidae and Vespertilionidae. Notable prevalences include Scotophilus kuhlii at 54% and S. heathii at 4%; Cynopterus brachyotis at 42%; Hipposideros cf. grandis at 23%; Taphozous melanopogon (emballonurid) at 18%. Infections newly recorded in Megaerops niphanae and Eonycteris spelaea; no infections detected in Molossidae, Megadermatidae or Rhinolophidae (sampling limits). Phylogenetics show Polychromophilus as a conserved Cambodian–Thai–Madagascar lineage, while Hepatocystis exhibits deep divergence with possible historical bat–rodent host shifts in Asia, revealing extensive, underrecognized malaria parasite diversity in Southeast Asia.

article.articleHeadline: In a thousand-year-old religious text, traces of an ancient disease were found.
article.articleSummary: Researchers from University College Dublin report finding traces of sheep pox in the York Gospels, a 1000-year-old manuscript. Published in Science Advances, the study traces the evolution of the sheep pox virus using ancient DNA preserved in manuscripts and animal remains. Sheep pox is highly contagious among sheep and can devastate flocks, with high mortality in young animals; humans are not generally affected. DNA of the virus was detected on parchment made from calf and goat skins, suggesting interspecies infection or contamination during parchment production. Comparison with Bronze Age sheep teeth DNA shows sheep pox has affected domestic stock for more than 3700 years across Eurasia. The York Gospels were written in Canterbury in the late 10th century and later housed at York Minster. The findings imply parchment archives worldwide may harbor historical pathogen DNA, aiding understanding of viral evolution and informing eradication efforts, including Greece's current outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: Venezuelan boy 'predicted' the plague; what is known about the death in Irkutsk.

The World Health Organization has requested complete risk information, and the U.S. embassy has warned citizens to leave Russia, elevating travel advisory to level 4. Independent Russian media speculate infection from a broken test tube in a laboratory at the Irkutsk Pest Research Institute or during a trip to Thailand. The case has amplified social-media interest in a Venezuelan boy, Jesús López, aka “El Servidor,” whose September 29 prophecy about pestilence and death sparked comparisons to Shipilova’s death. Experts emphasize no scientific basis for these predictions, attributing viral spread to algorithmic amplification rather than facts.

article.articleHeadline: Buriram shaken! 5-year-old dies after suspected hand, foot and mouth disease; condition worsened within 3 days; Department of Disease Control warns of 4 danger signs.
article.articleSummary: Buriram, Thailand — a 5-year-old girl died after suspected hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD); deterioration occurred within three days of onset after returning from school. The Department of Disease Control is investigating, collecting samples for laboratory confirmation and analyzing Enterovirus strains, with emphasis on Enterovirus 71 due to risks of severe complications such as encephalitis and myocarditis. Common circulating HFMD strains Coxsackievirus A6 and A16 are typically milder; Enterovirus 71 accounts for about 5–15% of detections annually and is linked to fatalities. National surveillance reports 81,829 HFMD cases and 1 death (age 2y10m) from Jan 1–Oct 5, 2569 BE (2026), with 7,802 hospitalizations. Highest incidence provinces: Chiang Rai, Chonburi, Bangkok. Preventive measures in schools: strict daily screening, isolate ill children, close classrooms if 2+ cases in a week, thorough cleaning, and rigorous hand hygiene; hotline 1422.

article.articleHeadline: AI-Powered X-Ray Screening Proves Feasible for TB Detection in
article.articleSummary: TB remains the deadliest infectious disease; in 2024 the Philippines accounted for 6.8% of the global TB caseload, underscoring transmission in crowded urban settings. A qualitative study in PLOS Global Public Health evaluates AI-powered CAD (computer-aided detection) applied to digital chest X-ray during a Médecins Sans Frontières community active case finding campaign in Tondo, Manila. From January to April 2023, in-depth interviews and observations with MSF staff, local clinicians, program personnel, and residents explored perceptions beyond diagnostic accuracy. Four themes emerged: (1) operational efficiency—CAD increased screening capacity and streamlined workloads; (2) human resources and role adaptation—reallocating tasks required ongoing training and support; (3) technical feasibility and system design—calibrating probability thresholds depends on local prevalence and health-system capacity; (4) community acceptability and ethics—trust grows when technology is embedded in accessible, not parachuted, care.

article.articleHeadline: Shorter High-Dose Antibiotic Course for Buruli Ulcer Shows Promise but
article.articleSummary: Buruli ulcer in Ghana was studied in the SHARP randomized trial, testing whether four weeks of high-dose rifampicin (20 mg/kg) plus clarithromycin (15 mg/kg) could match eight weeks of standard-dose therapy (rifampicin 10 mg/kg with clarithromycin). All PCR-confirmed cases received wound dressings coated with dialkylcarbamoyl chloride. Primary endpoint: time until no viable Mycobacterium ulcerans detected by quantitative PCR targeting 16S rRNA, followed through week 20. From Nov 2021 to Jul 2024, 42 participants were randomized (23 high-dose, 19 standard). Mean clearance times were 4.9 vs 7.0 weeks; adjusted difference 0.5 weeks in favor of the short course, p=0.835, with CI crossing null. Paradoxical reactions: 0/21 in high-dose vs 5/15 in standard; OR 0.19, p=0.102. No recurrences in either arm; safety was similar. Conclusion: no clear microbiological advantage for the four-week regimen; larger trials are needed.

article.articleHeadline: Ghana Pilots Simple Home-Visit Checklist to Find Hidden Tropical Diseases
article.articleSummary: Ghana piloted a simple home-visit checklist to detect neglected tropical diseases (NTDs). Sixty-four Community Health Officers across Kassena Nankana West (north), Nkwanta South (middle belt) and Ga South (coastal) conducted 1,932 household visits from September to December 2023, generating over 1,100 suspected case observations. Using seven syndromic indicators—blood in urine; skin lesions; visible deformities; eye complications; lymphoedema or limb swelling; suspected hydrocele; and deep skin wounds with undermined edges—mapped to urogenital schistosomiasis, lymphatic filariasis, onchocerciasis, trachoma, yaws, scabies or leprosy morbidity. Skin lesions dominated (1,117 observations). Ga South produced 75% of blood-in-urine reports; Kassena Nankana West contributed 80.8% of lymphoedema and 67.5% of eye conditions; visible deformities concentrated in Ga South; deep wounds clustered in Nkwanta South and Ga South. Uptake of protocols exceeded 85% among trained workers, illustrating frontline surveillance feasibility to inform targeted resource allocation under the WHO 2021–2030 NTD roadmap.

article.articleHeadline: Cat Litter and Pregnancy: Toxoplasma Parasite Found in Over 40 Percent of
article.articleSummary: In eastern Ghana's Volta Region, a cross-sectional study at Ho Teaching Hospital found that 42.5% of 201 pregnant women at their first antenatal visit tested positive for Toxoplasma gondii antibodies (85/201). Among positives, 96.5% were IgG-only (dormant tissue cysts) and 3.5% had IgG and IgM (possible recent or reactivated infection). Blood samples were screened for T. gondii–IgG/IgM by rapid test; participants were enrolled Feb 24–Apr 7, 2025. Regression identified parity as a key risk: primiparous (OR 3.93, 95% CI 1.42–10.91) and multiparous (OR 3.85, 95% CI 1.50–9.87) vs nulliparous. Most exposures are prior immunity, reducing fetal transmission risk, yet more than half remain susceptible to primary infection during pregnancy. T. gondii is transmitted via cat feces–derived oocysts, undercooked meat, or contaminated food, water, or soil; findings raise discussion on routine antenatal screening in Ghana.

article.articleHeadline: Analysis: Ghana's yellow fever numbers reveal a gap between vaccination and protection
article.articleSummary: Ghana recorded about 450 suspected yellow fever cases from June–September 2026, including 74 in the Upper West Region and three laboratory-confirmed infections. The data highlight the gap between suspected and confirmed cases, and between vaccination and verified immunity, as no national breakdown of confirmed/negative/pending results has been released. Yellow fever is mosquito-borne; vaccination is the key protection. Past data show 235 Ghanaian cases reported 2021–2025, but 450 suspected in 2026 are not directly comparable due to differing case definitions. Upper West has prior outbreak history; Wa East (2021) involved 57 suspected, 12 confirmed and four deaths, with vaccination in the district rising from 25% to 95% after mass campaigns. National routine vaccination estimates: 94% (2021), 95% (2022), 88% (2023), 91% (2025). The International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP) records vaccination but does not guarantee protection; gaps arise if certificates are falsified or lost, though one-dose vaccination is generally lifelong.

article.articleHeadline: Sugar Bait Traps Fail to Curb Malaria in Landmark Three-Country Trial
article.articleSummary: Malaria control using attractive targeted sugar baits (ATSB) with Westham Sarabi v1.2 failed to reduce malaria in three large Phase III trials conducted in Kenya, Mali, and Zambia. The bait stations used 0.11% dinotefuran and were mounted two per house on exterior walls. Across nearly 7,000 child-years, and 6,981 person-years for clinical malaria incidence, the study found no statistically significant differences between intervention and control for clinical malaria, Plasmodium falciparum infection prevalence, or four entomological measures (parity, mosquito abundance, landing rate, sporozoite positivity) in Anopheles. A post-hoc analysis revealed a dose-response: each additional 10 bait stations per hectare correlated with a 19% reduction in clinical malaria incidence (IRR 0.81; 95% CI 0.74-0.89; p<0.001), but only when baits were in good condition. Implication: deployment density and bait maintenance may determine efficacy; thresholds remain undetermined. Methodological lessons for future cluster trials.
